themes_detail.label: Lead Inspections Surge
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints spiked to 5 reports last week (1900% above the 8-week average of 0.2 per week), signaling a potential cluster of lead exposure cases in Fordham/University Heights that warrants immediate investigation into whether this reflects newly discovered contamination, renovation-related disturbance, or a reporting surge tied to a specific building or school.
evidence: 5 lead complaints filed last week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1900% spike, z-score 10.97)
Lead is a known health crisis in NYC with disproportionate impact on low-income communities and children
Fordham/University Heights has aging housing stock (251 building permits filed in last 90 days, 136 alterations—renovation activity may disturb lead paint)
reporting_angles: Investigate whether the spike is tied to a specific building, school, or renovation project; interview DOH to understand source
Examine how many children in the district have been tested for lead and what the results show; profile affected families

themes_detail.label: Mysterious SPIT Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints exploded to 5 reports this week versus a near-zero 8-week baseline (3900% spike, z-score 14.74), indicating either a newly emergent code violation crisis or a reporting artifact that needs urgent clarification from DOB.
evidence: 5 SPIT complaints filed this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3900% spike, z-score 14.74, highest severity flagged)
SPIT handles complex building code violations and structural issues—the scale of this spike suggests a coordinated inspection sweep or multi-site problem
251 building permits filed in last 90 days (136 alterations) indicates active construction; SPIT complaints may reflect code enforcement on ongoing work
reporting_angles: Contact DOB immediately to clarify what SPIT complaints mean and whether this reflects a specific enforcement action or genuine uptick in violations
Map the 5 complaints to specific buildings and block numbers to identify whether they cluster around a single project or neighborhood

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Eruption
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged to 262 reports two weeks ago, a 309% spike above the 8-week average of 64 complaints per week (z-score 3.67), indicating a sustained noise problem—likely tied to construction, street work, or nightlife—that is degrading quality of life in a densely populated neighborhood.
evidence: 262 street/sidewalk noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 64 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (309% spike, z-score 3.67)
Street/Sidewalk Noise is the 6th-highest complaint category overall (1,018 complaints over 90 days), indicating chronic problem
251 active building permits filed in last 90 days suggests ongoing construction activity that may be generating noise at off-hours
reporting_angles: Survey residents and local businesses about the timing and sources of noise; identify whether it's tied to specific construction sites or venues
Request DOB and FDNY records on any after-hours work permits or complaint patterns; investigate whether enforcement is adequate

themes_detail.label: Drinking Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Drinking-related complaints jumped to 3 reports two weeks ago, a 2300% spike above the 8-week baseline of 0.1 per week (z-score 8.69), suggesting a potential cluster of public intoxication or alcohol-related street activity that may require NYPD outreach or substance abuse intervention.
evidence: 3 drinking complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Fordham is home to Fordham University and multiple bars; spike may reflect seasonal nightlife increase or new venue opening
No corresponding Reddit discussions or news coverage yet, suggesting this issue may not yet be on community radar
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD and community board to understand whether spike represents real behavioral change or increased reporting
Map the 3 complaints by location; check if they cluster near bars, parks, or transit hubs; interview residents about public safety concerns

themes_detail.label: Water Conservation Alerts
themes_detail.summary: Water conservation complaints jumped to 6 reports two weeks ago, a 433% spike above the 8-week average of 1.1 per week (z-score 5.26), potentially indicating water shortage fears, broken hydrants, or infrastructure leaks that may require investigation by DEP.
evidence: 6 water conservation complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (433% spike, z-score 5.26)
Water Leak complaints also elevated at 642 total over 90 days, suggesting infrastructure stress in the district
HEAT/HOT WATER remains the #1 311 complaint category at 4,775 complaints over 90 days—water system issues are persistent in this district
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to determine if there are active water main breaks, hydrant leaks, or pressure issues in the district
Interview residents about water quality and pressure; check whether spike coincides with any city water advisory or maintenance work
